result.bottom_line: Gauge flood history is feasible as a narrow first-version layer, not as a daily flood-day history. NWPS lists 277 Montana gauges; 102 define an NWS flood stage and 57 define all four categories. The Billings gauge (BILM8, USGS 06214500, flood stage 13.5 ft) is 2.0 miles from the town centre, and its USGS annual peak stage runs from water year 1963 to 2024. Water year 2022 is the only year in 2021 to 2025 at or above flood stage: 2 days (2022-06-14 and 2022-06-15), 170 fifteen-minute readings at or above 13.5 ft, and a peak of 16.37 ft at 09:30 MDT on 2022-06-15. Neither USGS service has a daily gage height series for this gauge, so daily flood-day counts would have to be built from 15-minute data. The requested endpoint (waterservices.usgs.gov) is being shut down on 2027-02-22 and slowed from 2026-11-16; api.waterdata.usgs.gov answered all 109 anonymous requests tested. Only 17.3 percent of Montana grid points lie within 10 miles of a flood-stage gauge; 12 of the 14 towns in towns.json do.
result.recommendation: IN for the first version, narrowed to one line per location: the nearest gauge with an NWS flood stage within 10 miles, its NWS flood categories, and its USGS annual peak stage by water year (98 of the 99 Montana flood-stage gauges with a USGS number have one, earliest water year 1894). Build it from api.waterdata.usgs.gov and NWPS. Bytes: the compact peak table for those 98 gauges is 207,359 bytes raw (54,253 gzipped; 7,116 rows); raw downloads for this study totalled 37,245,565 bytes. OUT for v1: daily flood-day counts and 15-minute stage histories (no daily stage series exists; about 2.75 MB raw JSON per gauge per water year, roughly 1.4 GB raw for 99 gauges over five water years). Legal basis: NWS and USGS data are US government works (17 U.S.C. section 105(a)); NWS pages are public domain for any lawful purpose on three conditions (no claim of ownership, no implied NWS endorsement, no modified content presented as official), the NWS name and visual identifier are trademark-protected, and USGS asks for credit. Per-address lines wait behind the counsel gate in the hail research README section 8.3 (OW-H7); a per-town gauge table could ship first. Official flood warnings (IEM FL.W) are a separate lane: the June 2022 record is usable (14 NWS text products, each with UGC codes and a LAT...LON polygon; polygon first, then county, per AGENTS.md rule 6), but IEM's terms conflict, so use the NWS text source or resolve IEM's terms first.

result.bottom_line: Split the data. Keep the 10-minute Website site small (static shell about 273 KB gzipped) and move the bulk data (about 358 MB raw, about 71 MB gzipped per full deploy) to a daily or monthly deploy of a second repository's own GitHub Pages site. A Pages site is replaced whole on every deploy, so bulk data kept in the 10-minute site would be re-uploaded up to 144 times a day. The 10-minute cadence is not delivered: 17 scheduled runs in 52.4 hours on main, median gap 151.5 minutes. hail-store.yml is not on main (404), so the daily store job is not scheduled.
result.recommendation:
1) Layout. Keep the 10-minute site to HTML, CSS, JS, fonts, basemap, data/map.json and a small per-town hail summary that the daily job writes. Stop the 10-minute build from downloading and copying the store (only branch builds with --hail-history do so today). The published release asset is 8.36 MB (B1); the B2 store tar is 12.9 MB; B2 plus addresses is 26.4 MB. Put the bulk data (hail store, address shards and search index, street tiles, footprint shards, climate tiles, snow and station files) in a new repository with its own project Pages site. Browsers fetch those files cross-origin: access-control-allow-origin * and gzip on JSON were measured on this repo's Pages site. One repository has one Pages Source setting (publishing-source doc), so a second Pages site needs a second repository. Keeping one site and skipping unchanged files saves only the copy and pack step (6.6 to 6.7 s for 138 MB measured); the upload and deploy still carry the whole site.
2) Cadence. Daily job (hail store, joins, climate day, 45 candidate station files): about 12 to 15 minutes (hail build 612 s in CI; joins 99 s local; climate day about 1.4 MB; stations 33.7 MB). Monthly job (addresses: 65.8 MB zip, build 37 s, verify 9 to 39 s; climate scaled month 41 to 57 MB, published 4 to 68 days after month end; NOHRSC season about 2.4 MB) and an annual or on-change streets and footprints job, each well under the 60-minute timeout.
3) Browser budget, Billings, 390x844 phone, zoom 15, gzip: shell 273 KB (estimate for fonts and map.json); one hail click 5 KB; dots 3,737 in 7 shards 87 KB; footprints 8 shards 193 KB; one street tile after 2 m simplification 49 KB. All layers total 607 KB, about 12 s on the Slow 3G preset plus round trips. With footprints from zoom 16 instead, 393 KB (about 8 s). Footprints at zoom 13 would be 797 KB and must not load there. Desktop 1280x800 at zoom 15: 735 KB. The repo states no 3G target; the owner must set one.
4) Egress. Fetching the 26.4 MB store on each of 144 runs a day would be about 3.8 GB a day; the observed 7.8 scheduled starts a day give about 0.2 GB. Browser transfer is about 0.6 MB per phone visit, so the 100 GB monthly soft limit is about 165,000 such visits.
5) Extraction and deploy. B2 alone: 54 MB, 9,372 files, extract 0.6 to 3.1 s. B2 plus addresses: 138 MB, 21,086 files, extract 8.7 to 13.6 s (file creation dominates). Full planned site: about 358 MB raw and about 36,600 files; extract about 15 to 25 s, pack about 17 to 20 s, and about 71 MB gzipped per 10-minute deploy (about 10 GB a day of uploads). Pages deploy time at this size was not measured; the upload action's README advises under 1 GB because larger deploys are more likely to exceed the 10-minute timeout.

B2 store drifted after the snapshot: tar.gz is now 12,876,467 B (record 12,876,200) and member bytes 54,227,125 (record 54,226,141). Entries and tile counts match.
Phone z15 total with the live shell is about 593 KB (record 607 KB). Footprint and address items remain estimates.
Reword 'a Pages site is replaced whole on every deploy' to 'each run uploads the whole site artifact'. No quoted page uses the replacement wording.
Omitted term: the Pages limits page says 'GitHub Pages source repositories have a recommended limit of 1 GB'. The data repository should keep git content small and publish data as a build artifact.
Branch names: the record's 'hail-b1 branch' is claude/hail-b1 and 'desktop-app' is claude/desktop-app. No effect on the figures.
open_questions: The owner must set the 3G target. The repo defines none; figures use the DevTools Slow 3G preset (about 50 KB/s, 400 ms round trip).

The 10-minute cron on main does not deliver 10-minute runs (median gap 151.5 minutes). Whether an external trigger would fix it was not tested; the owner needs to accept the observed cadence or change the trigger.
hail-store.yml is absent on main, so the daily store job does not run until it is merged to the default branch.
Pages deploy time for a 358 MB site was not measured; the upload action advises under 1 GB because larger deploys risk the 10-minute timeout.
Second-site headers were checked only on this repo's project site; the new data repository's headers must be checked on its first deploy.
The GitHub Pages sentence about online businesses (quoted in terms) needs a reading against this site's purpose by the owner or counsel.
Footprint geodatabase read and whole-state street simplification and tile writes were not timed; the streets record's MSL pipeline took 629 s, a different input.
Tile grids differ: the B1 hail grid has tile edges at whole tenths of a degree; the streets record uses edges at 0.05-degree offsets. One grid should be chosen before sharding.
The climate record's 25,902 land cells replaces the brief's 30,000; five-year climate sizes use one record per cell written five times as a stand-in, and the aggregate cache size is an estimate.
The B3 address folder was being rebuilt during measurement; figures agree across 03:04 to 03:14 UTC within 0.2 percent. The precheck shows 4,212 shards and 43.5 MB; the build shows 4,211 and 43.1 MB.
TIGER edition is named two ways (2025 and 2026); zip totals differ by 809 bytes, so the size estimate does not change.
The Microsoft footprint alternative (773,199 polygons, ODbL share-alike) has a record estimate of about 119 MB at 5 decimals, not a file measurement.
